# Isolated fstool development fork

Milestone40 adds a read-only loaded-catalog check for unsupported per-record
expanded dates, called by the production adapter before file access. The bridge
also rejects unsupported volume flags. See [format guards](../docs/FORMAT-GUARDS.md).

Milestone39 updates the volume writer identity and write counter together with
metadata publication and preserves bytes during unchanged flushes. See
[generation checks and acceptance](../docs/VOLUME-GENERATION.md).

Milestone28 adds `hfs_plus/reclamation.rs` and calls it from the shared removal
preflight. Data/resource extents must have valid allocated coverage and no
overlap with another owner, reserved metadata, journal or fork-backed attribute
before deletion, replacement or deferred reclamation can proceed. See
[ownership validation](../docs/DELETION-OWNERSHIP.md). Earlier milestone counts
and limits below describe their historical source snapshots.

The `fstool/` directory was copied from the published crates.io fstool 0.4.35 package, whose selected files were SHA-256 matched to research revision `67a97d2971d8559b5defcdeba6bd0c71ba625f17`. The published package records VCS revision `c38a130f6099b929cf0d7001a692d619311243c4`; matching selected source does not imply that the entire revisions are identical. The original package SHA-256 is recorded in `artifacts/milestone-2/upstream-package.json`. Original registry and research evidence copies remain unchanged. Cargo's local patch selects this fork; Cargo.lock retains the exact dependency versions. Upstream licences and attribution are retained.

Milestone 2 modified journal.rs and writer.rs. Milestone 3 also modifies mod.rs and attributes.rs; milestone 4 adds handle.rs. Milestone 5 modifies catalog.rs and adds unicode.rs/unicode_data.rs. Milestone 6 updates handle/writer/journal/mod for touched-block replacement, original catalog-leaf patches, and changed-sector transactions. Milestone 7 adds catalog_update.rs for localized structural catalog changes; milestone 9 adds attribute_delete.rs. Current comparison covers all 331 published files and the 335-file fork: six existing files differ, four are added and none are missing. See `artifacts/milestone-10/vendor-diff.json` and `vendor-comparison.json`; earlier manifests remain historical.

- Correct in-filesystem journal flag from 2 to 1.
- Fail on missing/unsupported journal-info settings instead of silently selecting direct writes.
- Flush journal payload/new file data before publishing the committed end pointer.
- Accept one complete, aligned metadata batch per commit. Reject a batch exceeding the ring or block-list capacity before writes. Equality with ring capacity is rejected because it aliases the empty-journal state.
- Clear formatter-only journal initialization fields after the first successful flush so subsequent flushes cannot reset a live journal.
- Validate all committed replay records before applying any home blocks, including payload checksums, alignment, committed-range limits, and prohibition on targeting the journal itself.
- Write loaded journal headers as one complete logical sector.
- Add staged, non-replacing rename/move with stable CNID/body, thread rekeying, checked parent valences, case-only HFS+ handling, HFSX comparison, cycle checks, and immutable/append-only/name-locked refusal.
- Preserve existing volume-header dates, clump values, encoding bitmap, Finder info and persistent UUID rather than regenerating defaults on each flush. Writer-owned allocation/count/fork fields still regenerate. Milestone39 supersedes the earlier write-count preservation: genuine metadata publications advance it and identify the writer.
- Decode modern inline `HFSPlusAttrData` using two reserved u32 words and attrSize at byte 12. Upstream used the obsolete twelve-byte prefix. Matching upstream test builders were corrected; root tests independently encode the modern layout.
- Replace existing-file in-place writes with touched-block copy-on-write and shared unchanged extents. Detached committed/private blocks remain allocated through shrink/regrow until fork publication and unused-block retirement occur in one metadata transaction. Preserve clump size, identity, resource forks and other catalog fields. Bounded copy scratch and temporary replacement space are required. Milestone 4 initially copied the whole retained fork; milestone 6 narrows replacement to touched blocks.
- Check offset arithmetic, zero-fill holes/extensions, validate data-fork coverage, refuse unsupported/locked entries, and require reopening after failed edits/flushes. Suppress implicit close retries after failure. Reject pending journals before attaching a handle to its cached catalog. Remove the journal-overlay helpers no longer needed by the private-fork editor.
- Normalize public path/volume names with fixed BMP Unicode 3.2 canonical decomposition and ordering, HFS exceptions and algorithmic Hangul; preserve supplementary pairs. Validate the post-normalization length instead of truncating. Leave raw internal attribute constructors unchanged.
- Refuse equivalent destination names before staging catalog IDs or file data. Use the normalized volume-root name consistently in catalog keys, threads and cache state. Generated Unicode source, licence, references and hashes are retained in `research/evidence/unicode-3.2/`.
- Track original catalog record positions and changed keys. Patch existing fixed-size bodies in their leaf nodes, rechecking wire identity/geometry, and preserve unchanged tree layout. Existing-catalog structural changes use a staged localized planner for leaf/index splits, sibling links, merges, index redistribution, root collapse, freed-node reuse, fork growth and native map continuations. Preserve original header user/reserved fields. Refuse inconsistent visited tree boundaries/maps before publication. Install slot changes only after successful commit. The full builder remains for initial formatting. Skip unchanged overflow trees and update HFSX folder-count bodies only when changed.
- Map metadata node writes across inline extents, including nodes split between physical runs. Resolve overlapping journal writes before comparing final sectors and coalescing adjacent changes. Refuse dirty logs, invalid targets and oversized batches; no unaligned padding or split commits. Re-export a controlled low-level journal API for independent transaction tests while keeping geometry/internal mutation crate-private.
- Milestone 8 adds checked CNID/thread-to-forward-key identity lookup and ancestor paths, independent staging of four native catalog timestamps, and engine refusal of the HFS file-lock bit. These support the driver-independent Windows adapter while preserving existing BSD/Finder, backup-date and fork bytes. Native WinFsp/security integration remains open; see [adapter validation](../docs/WINDOWS-ADAPTER.md).
- Milestone 9 adds bounded inline-attribute deletion in a checked single-leaf tree, removing stale CNID-keyed records in the same transaction as catalog removal and fork retirement. Retained records stay verbatim; the last record leaves a valid empty tree. Larger attribute trees and fork-backed target values are refused before engine staging or Windows cleanup. The adapter separately adds a persistent deferred-reclamation protocol; see [format and limitations](../docs/DURABLE-DELETION.md).
- Milestone 10 generalizes inline deletion to checked multi-level trees, sparse IDs and continuation maps. It validates all live structure, preserves raw non-target records and header/user fields, and repacks within the existing reservation, publishing only changed nodes. Root/volume attributes remain intact. Attribute lookups use their own binary header comparison on HFS+ and HFSX; successful flush refreshes cached attribute headers and refresh errors poison the writer. Fork-backed targets remain refused; full repacking and journal capacity remain limits. Independent fixtures cover root collapse, malformed-tree refusal and raw retention; deferred-deletion persistence tests now exercise a deeper attribute tree.

These changes are a development milestone, not a complete filesystem safety audit. Multi-list writer transactions, generalized unaligned writes, native Mac interoperability, and hardware power-loss validation remain pending. The production image CLI still refuses a pending journal. Recovery writes occur only in the test simulator. No project distribution licence has been selected; the upstream MIT declaration and Apple-derived table licences need distribution review.

Format references: [Apple TN1150](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/technotes/tn/tn1150.html), [Apple HFSPlusAttrData definition](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/hfs/blob/main/core/hfs_format.h). The same upstream source before the journal patches failed the new crash simulator when a journal header persisted before its payload; the trace and original probe output are retained under `artifacts/milestone-2/`.

Milestone 12 adds native basic-info staging that preserves unrelated fields while mapping hidden, read-only and archive to existing HFS fields. The concrete private-fork handle now supports real allocation separately from EOF, including zero reservation and joint allocation/EOF shrink; the public FileHandle trait remains unchanged. The Windows adapter adds checked regular-file replacement before one flush. A fresh 92-test run and expanded 68-scenario engine matrix supersede the earlier baseline; genuine Mac and physical gates remain open. See docs/WINDOWS-BASIC-INFO.md.
